mainTopic: Whether a beehive counts as land, the impurity status of its honey, and how a buyer must cut down trees he bought for their wood.
overview: The amud opens with a משנה about a beehive. רבי אליעזר says it is like land, so a פרוזבול can be written on it, it cannot become impure in its place, and taking honey from it on שבת earns a חטאת. חכמים disagree on every point. רבי אלעזר finds רבי אליעזר's source in the words 'יערת הדבש': honey is like a forest, so taking it is like picking from a tree. Two ברייתות then challenge רבא's explanation of honey that is 'not food and not liquid.' The first is answered by saying the honey flowed onto something disgusting or onto straw. The second is answered by reading the ברייתא the other way. A ברייתא is also brought that supports רב כהנא. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about buying trees for cutting and brings a ברייתא on how high the buyer must cut each kind of tree. אביי explains why a sycamore needs three טפחים, which does not clash with the rules of שביעית. Finally, the claim that a cedar does not regrow is challenged from a פסוק about the צדיק. The answer is that 'cedar' covers ten kinds of trees, and the list of them continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: a beehive is like land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. In it, רבי אליעזר treats a beehive like land in three ways: פרוזבול, טומאה, and שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: About a beehive, רבי אליעזר says it is like land. So you may write a פרוזבול based on it. It does not become impure while it sits in its place. And someone who takes honey out of it on שבת must bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to support the point it was just discussing. The first half of the משנה gives רבי אליעזר's view that a beehive counts as land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling the beehive 'like land' leads to three results. A פרוזבול needs the borrower to own some land, and the beehive counts. Land never becomes impure, so neither does the hive. Taking honey out is like uprooting something from the ground, which is a מלאכה on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned (in a משנה). Used to bring a משנה as support.
A document that stops שביעית from cancelling a loan. It is written only if the borrower owns some land.
One who scoops out or removes (honey from the hive)
A sin-offering, brought for doing a forbidden מלאכה on שבת by mistake

steps.whyThisMatters: This one idea, that a hive is 'like land', affects many areas of הלכה at once: loans and שביעית, טומאה, and שבת.

phrases.english: As we learned: a beehive of bees —

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי הִיא כַּקַּרְקַע,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: it is like land,
and one may write a prosbol based on it,
phrases.notes: A פרוזבול needs the borrower to own some land, and here the hive counts as that land.

phrases.english: and it does not become impure while in its place,
phrases.notes: 'In its place' means while it is still sitting attached to the ground.

phrases.english: and one who takes honey from it on Shabbat is liable to bring a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to support the statement made just before this section began.
steps.raayaObject: The point under discussion just before this section, about the status of a beehive and its honey
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שביעית about a כוורת

steps.title: The Sages: a beehive is not like land
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree with רבי אליעזר. They treat the beehive as movable property in all three areas.
steps.simpleTranslation: But חכמים say: You may not write a פרוזבול based on it, and it is not like land. It can become impure even in its place. And someone who takes honey from it on שבת is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the opposing view of חכמים. They reverse each of רבי אליעזר's rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חכמים, the hive is מטלטלין, things that can be moved. So it does not qualify for a פרוזבול, it can become impure, and taking honey from it is not like uprooting from the ground. That is why there is no חטאת.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument rests on one question: is a beehive land or movable property? רבי אליעזר says land. חכמים say movable property.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין כּוֹתְבִין עָלֶיהָ פְּרוֹזְבּוּל,
phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: one may not write a prosbol based on it,
and it is not like land,
and it can become impure even in its place,
and one who takes honey from it on Shabbat is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A beehive is movable property: no פרוזבול, it can become impure, and there is no חטאת for taking honey on שבת.

steps.title: What is רבי אליעזר's reason?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks why רבי אליעזר treats a beehive like land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: What is רבי אליעזר's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר asks for the source behind רבי אליעזר's view. He is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling a beehive 'land' is surprising, since a hive can be picked up and moved. So רבי אלעזר looks for a source that explains it.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the two names. רבי אֶלְעָזָר (an אמורא) is explaining the view of רבי אֱלִיעֶזֶר (the תנא in the משנה). They look and sound alike, but they are two different people.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first opinion in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for treating a beehive like land

steps.title: Honey is compared to a forest
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק calls a honeycomb 'יערת הדבש', a forest of honey. So honey in a hive is like fruit on a tree, and taking it on שבת makes one liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And he dipped it in the יערת הדבש.' What does a forest have to do with honey? It comes to teach you this: picking from a forest on שבת earns a חטאת, and in the same way, scooping honey from a hive on שבת earns a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers his own question with a פסוק. Because honey is linked to a forest, taking honey counts like picking from something growing in the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The odd word 'יער' (forest) next to honey tells us honey in its hive is like something attached to the ground. Picking from a tree is תולש, uprooting, which is a מלאכה on שבת. So רודה, scooping out honey, is the same, and this supports the view that the hive is like land.

keyTerms.meaning: What does this have to do with...? A question that shows a word must be teaching something.
One who picks or uproots (from something attached to the ground)
Just as ... so too. Used to build a comparison.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's view that a hive is land comes from the words 'יערת הדבש'. Honey in the hive is like fruit on a tree, so taking it on שבת is like picking.
steps.whyThisMatters: The forest comparison is why רבי אליעזר treats the hive as attached to the ground, and that is behind all three of his rulings.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And he dipped it in the honeycomb" —

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה עִנְיַן יַעַר אֵצֶל דְּבַשׁ?
phrases.english: Now what does a forest have to do with honey?
phrases.notes: The word for honeycomb here sounds like 'forest' (יער), and that is what the question is about.

phrases.english: Rather, it is to tell you:

phrases.aramaic: מָה יַעַר – הַתּוֹלֵשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ בְּשַׁבָּת חַיָּיב חַטָּאת,
phrases.english: just as with a forest, one who picks from it on Shabbat is liable to a sin-offering,

phrases.aramaic: אַף דְּבַשׁ – הָרוֹדֶה מִמֶּנּוּ בְּשַׁבָּת חַיָּיב חַטָּאת.
phrases.english: so too with honey, one who takes it out on Shabbat is liable to a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of רבי אלעזר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק links honey to a forest. Taking honey from a hive is like picking from a tree, so it is a מלאכה on שבת and the hive is treated as attached to the ground.

steps.title: Honey that flowed out of the hive is still not food
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says honey that flows out of its hive is neither food nor liquid. This fits אביי but is hard for רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: A ברייתא says honey that flows out of its beehive is neither food nor liquid. This works for אביי, but it is a problem for רבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to challenge רבא. Honey that has already flowed out of the hive is still called 'not food and not liquid.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי can say this is the honey left for the bees, which nobody plans to eat, so it is not food. רבא said the reason is רבי אליעזר's view that a hive is like land. Once the honey has flowed out of the hive, even רבי אליעזר would not call it attached to land, so why is it still not food?

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection from a ברייתא
Food (food can become טמא as food)
Liquid (liquids can become טמא as liquid)
Granted for this opinion, but for that opinion it is a problem

steps.confusionAlert: The word הַזָּב here simply means 'flowing out.' It has nothing to do with the זב of טומאה.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Honey that flows out of its beehive
is neither food nor liquid.
Granted, according to אביי it works out fine;
phrases.notes: אביי can say this is the honey left in the hive to feed the bees.

phrases.english: but according to רבא, it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the honey-and-land discussion to test רבא's earlier explanation against a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation that 'not food and not liquid' follows רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Honey that has flowed out is no longer in the hive, so the 'hive is like land' reason cannot explain why it is not food

steps.title: The honey flowed onto a disgusting vessel
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד answers that the honey flowed into a repulsive vessel, so it became unfit to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: It is talking about honey that flowed onto a disgusting vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד defends רבא. He explains the ברייתא as a special case where the honey landed somewhere gross.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason the honey is not food is not about land at all. It landed in a disgusting vessel, so people would not eat it. That makes it 'not food' for a completely different reason, and רבא's explanation is not challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, in a case where

phrases.english: רב זביד said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁזָּב עַל גַּבֵּי כְּלִי מָאוּס.
phrases.english: For example, where it flowed onto a disgusting vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by narrowing the case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The honey is not food because of where it came from (the hive)
steps.terutzMaskana: The honey is not food because it fell into something repulsive and nobody would eat it

steps.title: The honey flowed onto straw
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב gives a similar answer: the honey flowed onto straw and became inedible.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: It is talking about honey that flowed onto straw.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives another way to defend רבא, with a different example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רב זביד, he says the honey is ruined by where it landed. Here it is straw instead of a disgusting vessel, but the idea is the same: the honey is now unfit to eat, so it is not food.
steps.whatToRemember: Both answers keep רבא's view safe by saying the flowing honey was ruined by where it landed, not because of the hive.

phrases.english: רב אחא בר יעקב said:
For example, where it flowed onto straw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel answer to step 6 with a different example
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The honey is not food because of the hive
steps.terutzMaskana: The honey is not food because the straw made it inedible

steps.title: Honey in the hive becomes food once a person plans to eat it
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says honey in the hive is not food or liquid, but once a person plans to use it, it can become טמא. This fits אביי but is hard for רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: Honey in its hive is neither food nor liquid. If a person planned to eat it, it can become טמא as food. If he planned to use it as a liquid, it can become טמא as a liquid. This works for אביי, but it is a problem for רבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא against רבא. It says that a person's plan to eat the honey changes its status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי can say this is the bees' honey: once the owner decides to eat it after all, it counts as food. For רבא, a plan should not help according to רבי אליעזר, because something attached to land does not become food just by planning. So the ברייתא does not seem to follow רבי אליעזר, and רבא is left with a difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: He intended, planned (to use it a certain way)
The kind of טומאה that food can get
The kind of טומאה that liquids can get

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a person's intention can change the halachic status of an item. This is the central point the second ברייתא raises against רבא.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Honey in its beehive
is neither food nor liquid.
If he planned to use it as food,
it can become טמא with food טומאה.
phrases.notes: Literally 'it makes טמא,' but here it means the honey itself can now receive טומאה.

phrases.english: If he planned it as a liquid, it can become טמא with liquid טומאה.
Granted, according to אביי it works out fine;
but according to רבא, it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רבא, after the first one was answered
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation that 'not food and not liquid' follows רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי אליעזר, a plan alone should not turn attached honey into food. Yet the ברייתא says a plan does make it food, so it cannot be following רבי אליעזר

steps.title: רבא rereads the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the ברייתא should be read the opposite way: even if a person intends to use honey in its hive as food or drink, it still cannot become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא could answer you: read the ברייתא like this. If he planned to eat it, it does not become impure as food. If he planned to drink it, it does not become impure as a liquid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends himself against the challenge from step 8 by changing how we read the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seemed to say that intention makes the honey able to become טמא, which fits אביי. רבא reads it as saying the opposite: intention does not help. According to רבי אליעזר, honey in the hive is like fruit still attached to the ground, and attached things cannot become טמא even if someone plans to eat them. So the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, just as רבא said.

keyTerms.meaning: Fix it / answer it like this. The גמרא is about to reread a source.
He intended or planned something for the item.
The kind of impurity that food can get.
The kind of impurity that liquids can get.

phrases.english: Rava could say to you:
Answer it like this:
phrases.notes: רבא is changing how we read the ברייתא from step 8. He is not quoting a new source.

phrases.english: If he intended it for eating,
it does not become impure with the impurity of food;
if he intended it for liquids,
it does not become impure with the impurity of liquids.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8 against רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: 'it does become טמא' becomes 'it does not become טמא'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says intention lets honey in the hive become טמא, which fits only אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read correctly, the ברייתא says even intention does not let it become טמא, which fits רבא.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not bringing a different ברייתא. He is reading the same ברייתא from step 8 with the opposite result.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב כהנא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that honey in its hive can become טמא as food even without any intention, which matches רב כהנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רב כהנא: honey in its hive becomes impure as food even without intention.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב כהנא's view about honey in the hive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here honey in the hive needs no intention at all. It counts as food on its own and can become טמא as food. This is a different view from the ברייתא of step 8, as רבא reread it in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita in accordance with Rav Kahana:
Honey in its beehive
becomes impure with the impurity of food
without intention.
phrases.notes: Most foods count as food without a special plan. This says honey in the hive is like that too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the honey discussion by bringing support for רב כהנא.
steps.raayaObject: רב כהנא's view that honey in its hive is food without intention.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: honey in its hive becomes impure as food without intention.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אליעזר, honey in the hive is like land, so it cannot become טמא even with intention (רבא's reading of the ברייתא). For חכמים, as רב כהנא says, it is food on its own and can become טמא without intention. אביי explains the 'not food' ברייתות as talking about the honey left for the bees.

steps.title: How high to cut a tree bought for felling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about olive trees and brings a ברייתא. Someone who buys a tree to cut down must leave enough of it so that it can grow back. The amount depends on the kind of tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: olive trees bought for cutting, he leaves two shoots. רבנן taught: one who buys a tree to cut must cut it one טפח above the ground. An untrimmed sycamore: three טפחים. A sycamore that was cut before: two טפחים. Reeds and vines: from the knot and up. Palms and cedars: he may dig and uproot them, because their trunks do not grow back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה about olive trees and adds a ברייתא with exact heights for cutting different trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer gets the wood, but the seller keeps the land and wants the tree to grow back. So the buyer must leave a stump high enough to regrow. Palms and cedars never regrow from the trunk, so leaving a stump would not help, and the buyer may uproot them completely.

keyTerms.meaning: Shoots or stumps left on the tree so it can regrow.
A handbreadth, a measure of about 8-10 cm.
A sycamore that has never been cut ('virgin sycamore').
A sycamore trunk that was already cut once and has strong roots.
The knot or joint on a reed or vine.

phrases.english: If one buys olive trees for cutting down,
he must leave two shoots.
The Rabbis taught:
One who buys a tree from his friend to cut down
goes up one handbreadth from the ground and cuts.
An untrimmed sycamore: three handbreadths.
A sycamore trunk already cut: two handbreadths.
With reeds and vines,
he cuts from the knot and upward.
With palms and cedars,
he may dig and uproot,
because their trunk does not grow back.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֵיתִים לָקוֹץ מַנִּיחַ שְׁתֵּי גְרוֹפִיּוֹת. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: back to the משנה, after the honey discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A buyer must cut a tree high enough for it to regrow. The height depends on the kind of tree. Trees that cannot regrow may be uprooted.

steps.title: Does a virgin sycamore really need three handbreadths?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the three-טפחים rule and starts quoting a משנה about שביעית. That משנה forbids cutting a בתולת השקמה because cutting it is work that helps the tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really need three טפחים for a בתולת השקמה? Here is a contradiction: one may not cut a בתולת השקמה during שביעית, because it is a form of working the tree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It opens a contradicting source, and the punchline comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During שביעית one may not do work that helps trees grow. The משנה says cutting a בתולת השקמה counts as that kind of work. This shows that cutting the tree helps it regrow. The next step will show the exact height that helps.

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction: two sources that seem to clash.
The seventh year, when working the land is forbidden.
Work on the land or tree that helps it grow.

phrases.english: And an untrimmed sycamore,
do we really need three handbreadths?!
But a contradiction was raised:
One may not cut an untrimmed sycamore during the Sabbatical Year,
because it is work.
phrases.notes: Cutting it makes it grow back stronger, so it counts as caring for the tree.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְתוּלַת הַשִּׁקְמָה שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים בָּעֵינַן? וּרְמִינְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the three-טפחים rule of the ברייתא in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that a בתולת השקמה must be cut three טפחים above the ground.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה in שביעית treats cutting this tree as helpful work. This begins to show that cutting it helps even without leaving three טפחים.

steps.title: Only cutting at ground level harms the sycamore
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that in שביעית one must cut at ten טפחים or at ground level. The גמרא learns from this that only ground-level cutting harms the tree, so any other cut helps it, even below three טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: cutting it the normal way is forbidden. Instead he cuts ten טפחים up, or cuts it down level with the ground. So only ground level is harmful to it, and any other cut is good for it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה and draws the inference that completes the challenge against the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שביעית one must cut in a way that does not help the tree, and ground level is listed as such a way. So only a cut right at the ground fails to help the tree regrow. This means one טפח should be enough, and the ברייתא's demand for three טפחים looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one: here, any other way of cutting.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
in its usual way it is forbidden;
rather, he goes up ten handbreadths and cuts,
or cuts it down level with the ground.
So it is only level with the ground that is harmful,
but any other way is good for it!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעִם הָאָרֶץ הוּא דְּקָשֵׁי, הָא אִידַּךְ מְעַלֵּי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the קשיא begun in step 12 by drawing the decisive inference.
steps.kashyaTarget: The three-טפחים rule for a בתולת השקמה in the ברייתא of step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only cutting at ground level harms the tree, then any cut above the ground helps it regrow. So the buyer should not need to leave three טפחים.
steps.confusionAlert: The ten-טפחים cut is not what the inference is about. The גמרא focuses on 'ground level' being the only harmful option, so anything above ground, even a little, helps.

steps.title: אביי explains three levels of cutting
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that cutting at three טפחים helps the tree, cutting at ground level surely harms it, and cutting in between neither helps nor harms much. For שביעית we need a cut that surely harms. For a sale we need a cut that surely helps.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: cutting at three handbreadths is good for the tree. Cutting at ground level surely harms it. Anywhere in between does not really harm it and does not really help it. For שביעית, we only do something that surely harms the tree. For buying and selling, we only do something that surely helps it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from step 13. He shows that the rule for שביעית and the rule for a sale do not clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that any cut except ground level helps the tree, so three טפחים seemed like too much to require. אביי adds a middle zone, between the ground and three טפחים, that does not clearly help or harm. שביעית needs a cut that surely harms, so a low cut in the middle zone is not allowed there, but a ground-level cut is. A sale needs a cut that surely helps, so the buyer must leave three טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: is good for it, helps it
is bad for it, harms it

steps.whatToRemember: There are three zones. Three טפחים helps the tree, ground level harms it, and in between does neither clearly. שביעית requires a sure harm. A sale requires a sure benefit.
steps.confusionAlert: The two rules are not in conflict. The middle zone fails both tests, because it is not a sure harm for שביעית and not a sure benefit for a sale.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
three handbreadths is good for it,
at ground level surely harms it;
from here onward,
phrases.notes: He means the space between the ground and three טפחים.

phrases.english: it does not really harm it,
and it does not really help it.
For שביעית, we do
something that surely harms it,
for buying and selling, we do
something that surely helps it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים מְעַלֵּי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cuts into three levels of effect, with a different requirement for each area of law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any cut except ground level helps the tree, so the three-טפחים rule for a sale seemed unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only three טפחים surely helps the tree, so a sale requires it. Among the low cuts, only ground level surely harms it, so that low cut is allowed in שביעית (רבי יהודה also allows cutting at ten טפחים).

steps.title: Palms and cedars may be uprooted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא: with palms and cedars, the buyer may dig out the whole tree, because their trunks do not grow back.
steps.simpleTranslation: With palm trees and cedars, he may dig and uproot them, because their trunks do not grow back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא. This is setting up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving a stump is only required when the stump will grow back into a tree. Since a palm or cedar trunk supposedly will not grow back, there is nothing to protect, and the buyer may take the whole tree.

keyTerms.meaning: their trunk does not grow back

phrases.english: With palms and cedars,
he digs and uproots,
because their trunk does not grow back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא quoted in step 11 and looks at its next line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Palms and cedars may be fully uprooted because their trunks do not grow back.

steps.title: Does a cedar's trunk really not grow back?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim about cedars by quoting רבי חייא בר לולייני. He asks why the פסוק compares a צדיק to both a palm and a cedar.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a cedar's trunk really not grow back? But רבי חייא בר לולייני taught: what is the meaning of the פסוק "A צדיק will flourish like a palm, he will grow like a cedar in Lebanon"? If it says palm, why does it need to say cedar? And if it says cedar, why does it need to say palm?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the ברייתא's claim that a cedar trunk does not grow back. It starts quoting a דרשה that will show otherwise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא assumes that each tree in the פסוק teaches something the other tree cannot. His answer, in the next step, will show which quality of the cedar the פסוק wanted.

phrases.english: And a cedar's trunk does not grow back?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא דְּרֵישׁ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר לוּלְיָינִי,
phrases.english: But רבי חייא בר לולייני expounded:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"A righteous one will flourish like a palm,
he will grow like a cedar in Lebanon"?

phrases.aramaic: אִם נֶאֱמַר תָּמָר לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר אֶרֶז,
phrases.english: If palm is said, why is cedar said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם נֶאֱמַר אֶרֶז לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר תָּמָר?
phrases.english: and if cedar is said, why is palm said?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶרֶז אֵין גִּזְעוֹ מַחְלִיף?! וְהָא דְּרֵישׁ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר לוּלְיָינִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 15 for cedars.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that a cedar's trunk does not grow back.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A דרשה on a פסוק assumes that the cedar has a quality the palm lacks, and that quality turns out to be regrowth.

steps.title: The cedar teaches that a צדיק grows back
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא explains that the palm shows a צדיק bears fruit, and the cedar shows a צדיק's trunk grows back. So a cedar's trunk does grow back, which contradicts the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the פסוק said only cedar and not palm, I would have said: just as a cedar does not make fruit, a צדיק does not make fruit. That is why it says palm. And if it said only palm and not cedar, I would have said: just as a palm's trunk does not grow back, a צדיק's trunk does not grow back. That is why it says cedar!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא answers his own question. His answer shows that the cedar's quality is that its trunk grows back, and this finishes the challenge against the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each tree fills a gap the other leaves. The palm bears fruit but does not regrow, while the cedar regrows but bears no fruit. Since the cedar was mentioned to teach regrowth, a cedar's trunk must grow back. That contradicts the ברייתא's line about cedars.
steps.whatToRemember: According to this דרשה, a palm bears fruit but does not regrow, and a cedar regrows but bears no fruit. This clashes with the ברייתא, which says a cedar's trunk does not grow back.

phrases.aramaic: אִילּוּ נֶאֱמַר אֶרֶז וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר תָּמָר –
phrases.english: Had it said cedar and not said palm,
I would have said:
just as a cedar does not make fruit,
so too a righteous one does not make fruit;
that is why it says palm.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם נֶאֱמַר תָּמָר וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר אֶרֶז,
phrases.english: And had it said palm and not said cedar,
I would have said:
just as a palm's trunk does not grow back,
so too a righteous one's trunk does not grow back;
that is why it says cedar!
phrases.notes: So the cedar must be a tree whose trunk grows back, and that is the problem for the ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילּוּ נֶאֱמַר אֶרֶז וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר תָּמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי חייא's דרשה, which completes the challenge from step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That a cedar's trunk grows back, against the ברייתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא בר לולייני's דרשה on תהלים 92:13.

steps.title: The ברייתא means other kinds of cedar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא, which said a cedar's trunk does not grow back, is talking about other kinds of cedar, not the regular cedar.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what are we dealing with here? With other types of cedars, in line with רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from Step 17. The cedar in the ברייתא is a different kind of cedar from the one the פסוק about the צדיק has in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources can be true because the word 'cedar' covers more than one kind of tree. The regular cedar, the one compared to a צדיק, grows back. The ברייתא is talking about other kinds of cedar whose trunks do not grow back.

keyTerms.meaning: What are we dealing with here? This phrase introduces a narrower reading of a source.

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a palm or cedar is no longer a tree you may dig out. It only explains which kind of cedar the ברייתא means.

phrases.english: Rather, what are we dealing with here?
With other types of cedars,
phrases.notes: These are cedar-family trees whose trunks do not grow back, unlike the regular cedar from Step 17.

phrases.english: in line with רבה בר רב הונא;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Steps 16 and 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the ברייתא refers to a different species within the category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's 'cedar' is the same tree as the cedar compared to a צדיק, so the two sources contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means other kinds of cedar that do not grow back. The regular cedar does grow back.

steps.title: There are ten kinds of cedar, learned from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא quotes the school of רב: there are ten kinds of cedar, learned from a פסוק in ישעיהו. The גמרא then translates each tree name in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה בר רב הונא said in the name of the school of רב: there are ten kinds of cedar. The פסוק says, 'I will place in the wilderness the cedar, the acacia, and the myrtle, and the oil tree I will set...' The גמרא then gives each tree's Aramaic name: ארז is ארזא, שיטה is תורניתא, הדס is אסא, עץ שמן is אפרסמא, ברוש is ברתי, תדהר is שאגא, and תאשור is שורבינא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the idea that 'cedar' includes many kinds of trees. It quotes a teaching that there are ten kinds of cedar and lists the trees from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'cedar' is a family of ten trees, it makes sense that some grow back and some do not. That is exactly what the answer in Step 18 needs. The tree names in the פסוק are translated into the Aramaic names people knew.

keyTerms.meaning: They say in the school of רב
Literally 'oil tree'; here explained as the balsam tree

phrases.english: As רבה בר רב הונא said,
they say in the school of רב:
There are ten kinds of cedars,
as it says: 'I will place in the wilderness the cedar,'
'the acacia, and the myrtle;'
'and the oil tree I will set, etc.'
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' points to the rest of the פסוק, which names ברוש, תדהר and תאשור. Those are the next trees explained.

phrases.english: 'Erez' means cedar.
'Shitta' means acacia.
'Hadas' means myrtle.
'Etz shemen' means balsam tree.
'Berosh' means juniper.
'Tidhar' means teak.
'And te'ashur' means cypress.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמְרִי בֵּי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source referred to in Step 18 ('in line with רבה בר רב הונא')
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of the school of רב, based on ישעיהו 41:19

steps.title: But the list has only seven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the פסוק lists only seven trees, not ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are only seven!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא counts the trees in the פסוק and finds only seven. That does not match the claim of ten kinds of cedar, so this step sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The school of רב said there are ten kinds of cedar, but the פסוק they rely on names only seven trees. Three are missing, and the גמרא needs to explain where they come from.

phrases.english: These are only seven!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the count in Step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that there are ten kinds of cedar
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק brought as the source names only seven trees, so it does not support the number ten.

steps.title: רב דימי adds three more kinds
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי says three more trees were added to the list: אלונים, אלמונים, and אלמוגים. The גמרא starts to translate them.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: they added to them אלונים, אלמונים, and אלמוגים. אלונים are pistachio trees, אלמונים are oaks, and אלמוגים are...
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי fills in the three missing trees so the list reaches ten. The גמרא begins giving the Aramaic name of each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seven trees from the פסוק plus these three make ten, which matches the teaching of the school of רב. The explanation of אלמוגים continues on the next daf.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל to בבל
A third tree added to the list; its meaning is given on the next daf

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'cedar' covers a family of ten trees. That is why the ברייתא can say a 'cedar' does not grow back, even though the regular cedar, compared to a צדיק, does.

phrases.english: When רב דימי came, he said:
They added to them:
Allonim, almonim, almugim.
Allonim are pistachio trees,
almonim are oaks,
almugim are...

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר הוֹסִיפוּ עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 20 about the missing three trees
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding information: three more species complete the list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the seven trees in the פסוק count, so there cannot be ten kinds of cedar.
steps.terutzMaskana: Three more trees were added to the seven, making ten.
